title_original: The Photographers Who Shaped Our Picture of New York

editorial_excerpt_zh: 走进 Aperture 位于上西区新空间的首展内部。

"在这张照片中，罗伯特·弗兰克将一个街角变成了一场关于姿态的研究。三个年轻人斜倚在可能是店面的墙壁旁；其中一人直面镜头，一人半藏在手后，另一人则看起来介于表演与疲惫之间。在他们身后，一块标牌警告“不要错过”（DON’T MISS），仿佛这座城市本身就在不断宣传下一场奇观，而他们面前栏杆上的尖刺则暗示着这场奇观可能带有危险边缘。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "弗兰克是一位居住在纽约的瑞士裔摄影师，他在拍摄这张照片时，正在发展那种将渗透进其1958年出版的图书《美国人》并重塑纪实摄影的、不安且失衡的风格。（该书于次年出版英文版，并于1968年由 Aperture 首次出版。）他倾向于日常场景，将其重新塑造成对这个国家充满探寻、不带感伤的肖像的一部分。20世纪50年代中期，下东区是一个稠密的移民社区，生活在门廊、人行正如弗兰克在2015年的一次采访中所说：“当我年轻的时候，我可以日复一日地四处走动，寻找照片。”", "links": [{"text": "The Americans", "url": Ballad of Sexual Dependency，1986/2021年）。致谢艺术家", "credit": "Aperture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "南·戈尔丁", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《小床上的特里希》（1979年）中，南·戈尔丁以惊人的直接性拍摄了一个房间：刺眼的头顶灯、一张行军床，以及一个身穿连衣裙和高跟鞋斜躺在床上的身影。杂乱的地板和临时凑合的家具带有一种艰难挣扎的闹市区生活的氛围：临时拼凑、亲密无间，对局外人来说往往高深莫测（inscrutable）。处，四处游荡寻找镜头里闪现的画面。正如弗兰克在2015年访谈中所言：“年轻时我能连续好几天在街区里走来走去，寻找画面。”（注：原文此处存在复本与轻微错位，按结构忠实还原原单元内容。）这里对应原文block:19:text:0翻译：在《小床上的特里希》（1979年）中，南·戈尔丁以惊人的直接性拍摄了一个房间：刺眼的顶灯、一张行军床，以及一个身穿连衣裙和高跟鞋斜倚其上的身影。杂乱的地板和简陋的陈设带有一种艰难市井生活的氛围：临时拼凑、亲密无间，对局外人而言往往难以捉摸。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "戈尔丁从青少年时期开始摄影，并在她生活其中的亚文化圈子内逐渐形成了自己的方法——起初在波士顿及其周边，1978年搬到纽约后又在那里继续。她没有选择从外部进行旁观，而是从由朋友和爱人组成的“选择的家庭”内部进行拍摄，以亲历体验的即时感记录下欲望、温柔、迷人与破碎。这些照片被制作成配有音乐的幻灯片，后来又收录在她具有里程碑意义的书籍《性依赖的叙事曲》（The Ballad of Sexual "text": "这幅影像收录于《女孩照片》（Aperture，2020年）中，该书汇集了艺术家创作于1997年至2002年间、如今已成为标志性的系列作品。最初由单一的青少年合作者开始的项目，最终演变成了尖锐的社会评论，颠覆了通常以男孩为主角的冒险故事。正如库兰德所言：“我将女孩们塑造成了一支由十几岁离家出走者组成的常备军，以对抗 patriarchal 理想。”", "links": of Lower Manhattan，2020年）© 艺术家，并致谢纽约霍华德·格林伯格画廊", "credit": "Aperture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丹尼·里昂", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在此场景中，丹尼·里昂拍摄了正在被清空的下曼哈顿——铸铁外墙依然挺立，原本狭窄的街道因建筑物的消失而骤然开阔，拆除后的废墟堆积在边缘。一个孤独的身影穿过画面，仿佛正走过一座已经化为记忆的城市。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "里昂1942年出生于纽约，是战后美国关键的纪实摄影师之一。他一直对处于压力下的社群和地方充满兴趣。在这里，他记录了诸如最初的世界贸易中心等庞大市政项目所要求的“贫民窟清理”，拍摄出的照片既像是档案又像是挽歌。Aperture于2020年出版的传真版《下曼哈顿的毁灭》重现了里昂最初于1969年出版的摄影集，将他当时的见证带给新的观众，并让我们记住了这座城市曾经拥有的市中心建筑。", "links": [{"text": "The Destruction of Lower Manhattan", "url": "https://store.aperture.org/products/danny-lyon-the-destruction-of-lower-manhattan"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "在这张照片中，苏菲·里维拉正面拍摄了一位服务员，紧凑的构图将其衬托在暗色墙壁前，使得一丝不苟的领结、西装翻领和白色围裙几乎呈现出戏服般的质感。被拍摄者的表情沉稳却难以捉摸——既有职业感、戒备，又带着一丝疲惫——而闪光灯则将其定格在原本可能被忽视的工作瞬间中。这张照片拍摄于纽约，当时里维拉正在发展植根于波多黎各裔纽约人（Nuyorican）生活的摄影风格，它将日常劳动变成了一次直接的相遇。这幅影像属于更广泛的肖像画和街头摄影作品序列，这些作品由女性主义和政治意识所塑造，坚定地认为尊严、复杂性和自我定义可以从普通的房间和日常琐事开始。", article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The inaugural installation at Aperture’s new space, Aperture Loves New York pays tribute to photographers who have shaped—and been shaped by—the city. Showcasing artists anchored in Aperture’s publishing history, the presentation brings together photographs alongside corresponding Aperture books that have advanced the medium of photography and captured the complex spirit of New York. Organized by Sarah Meister, Executive Director, the installation features photographs by more than twenty artists ranging from past to present—including Diane Arbus, Awol Erizku, Robert Frank, Justine Kurland, Stephen Shore, and more.", "links": [{"text": "Aperture Loves New York", "url": "https://aperture.org/exhibitions/aperture-loves-new-york/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://aperture.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Tina-barney-the-reception-1985.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Tina Barney, The Reception , 1985, from Family Ties (2024) Courtesy the artist and Olney Gleason, New York", "credit": "Aperture"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Tina Barney"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As she so often does, Tina Barney stages a familiar social ritual as a quiet psychological drama. In a wood-paneled room hung with paintings and ornamented with flowers, figures in formal dress seem gathered for celebration. Yet their gazes slide away from one another, and the seating arrangement feels oddly tense. What is happening beyond the frame that the women are paying attention to?", "links": [{"text": "Tina Barney stages a familiar social ritual", "url": "https://store.aperture.org/collections/aperture-loves-new-york/products/tina-barney-family-ties"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Barney is known for large-scale color photographs that look effortless but are carefully constructed, often using the language of the family portrait to reveal what manners can conceal: hierarchy, intimacy, impatience. Made in New York in the mid-1980s—an era of sharpened wealth, display, and social choreography—this picture turns privilege into a subject, and the “nice” occasion into something charged and unsettled."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://aperture.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Ernest-cole-untitled-harlem-1968-scaled.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Ernest Cole, Harlem, ca. 1968, from The True America (2024) © Ernest Cole Family Trust", "credit": "Aperture"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ernest Cole"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ernest Cole captures the city in motion: two women stride through the frame in bright patterned clothing, their faces crisp against a gentle smear of traffic and storefront signs. The slight blur of the street behind them and the one woman’s knowing look make Harlem feel fast, lived-in, charged. article_text:
The inaugural installation at Aperture’s new space, Aperture Loves New York pays tribute to photographers who have shaped—and been shaped by—the city. Showcasing artists anchored in Aperture’s publishing history, the presentation brings together photographs alongside corresponding Aperture books that have advanced the medium of photography and captured the complex spirit of New York. Organized by Sarah Meister, Executive Director, the installation features photographs by more than twenty artists ranging from past to present—including Diane Arbus, Awol Erizku, Robert Frank, Justine Kurland, Stephen Shore, and more.

Tina Barney

As she so often does, Tina Barney stages a familiar social ritual as a quiet psychological drama. In a wood-paneled room hung with paintings and ornamented with flowers, figures in formal dress seem gathered for celebration. Yet their gazes slide away from one another, and the seating arrangement feels oddly tense. What is happening beyond the frame that the women are paying attention to?

Barney is known for large-scale color photographs that look effortless but are carefully constructed, often using the language of the family portrait to reveal what manners can conceal: hierarchy, intimacy, impatience. Made in New York in the mid-1980s—an era of sharpened wealth, display, and social choreography—this picture turns privilege into a subject, and the “nice” occasion into something charged and unsettled.

Ernest Cole

Ernest Cole captures the city in motion: two women stride through the frame in bright patterned clothing, their faces crisp against a gentle smear of traffic and storefront signs. The slight blur of the street behind them and the one woman’s knowing look make Harlem feel fast, lived-in, charged. The neighborhood offers public space as both a backdrop and a pulse.

Cole had arrived in New York only a short time earlier, after fleeing South Africa in 1966 to publish House of Bondage (1967), his devastating photobook on apartheid (reissued by Aperture in 2022). Living in exile, he turned his camera toward Black life in America , attentive to style, dignity, and the everyday theater of the sidewalk. Seen in the turbulent late 1960s—after civil rights victories, at the height of the Black Power movement, yet amid ongoing struggle—this photograph suggests both joy and urgency.

Awol Erizku

In this image made for The New Yorker , Awol Erizku depicts three kufis designed by Ruth E. Carter for Spike Lee’s Malcolm X . Set against a roiling, clouded backdrop, the hats read like small constellations: carefully patterned, slightly luminous, and charged with the weight of history carried by everyday objects. The figures appear in profile, as if the camera has caught a passing formation rather than a posed tableau.

Erizku moves fluidly between editorial commissions and a studio practice that quotes and reroutes art-historical forms, pop vernacular, and spiritual iconography. He may be best known for his 2017 portrait of Beyoncé announcing her twin pregnancy, in which almost archetypal symbols—the pose, the flowers, the veil—make contemporary fame feel like a myth already living in our collective imagination.

Robert Frank

In this image, Robert Frank turns a street corner into a study of attitude. Three young people lean against what may be a storefront; one meets the camera head-on, one half-hides behind a hand, and one looks caught between performance and fatigue. Behind them, a sign warns “DON’T MISS,” as if the city itself were constantly advertising the next spectacle, while spikes on the railing in front of them hint that the spectacle could have an edge.

Frank, a Swiss-born photographer living in New York, made this picture while developing the restless, off-kilter style that would permeate his 1958 book The Americans and reshape documentary photography. (The book was published in English the following year, and first published by Aperture in 1968.) He gravitated toward everyday scenes, recasting them as part of a searching, unsentimental portrait of the country. In the mid‑1950s, the Lower East Side was a dense, immigrant neighborhood, where life played out on stoops, sidewalks, and thresholds like this one. As Frank said in a 2015 interview, “When I was young, I could walk around, day after day, and hunt for pictures.”

Nan Goldin

In Trixie on the cot (1979), Nan Goldin photographs a room with startling directness: a hard overhead light, a bar cot, and a figure resting on it in a dress and heels. The cluttered floor and improvised furnishings carry the atmosphere of hardscrabble downtown life: makeshift, intimate, often inscrutable to outsiders.

Goldin began photographing as a teenager and developed her approach within the subcultures she lived alongside—first in and around Boston, then in New York after moving there in 1978. Rather than looking in from the outside, she made pictures from within a “chosen family” of friends and lovers, recording desire, tenderness, glamour, and collapse with the immediacy of lived experience. Those pictures were turned into slideshows that were accompanied by music, and later into her landmark book The Ballad of Sexual Dependency , a visual diary that helped redefine documentary intimacy.

Justine Kurland

In Playground (1998), Justine Kurland turns an everyday New York scene into something quietly cinematic: a small group of girls clustered around the swings, one in motion, the others seemingly engaged in the serious, shifting politics of attention and belonging. The picture is a familiar city space, but it also hints at a world the girls control—they’re watched, but not fully available.

This image appears in Girl Pictures (Aperture, 2020), which gathers the artist’s now-iconic series made between 1997 and 2002. What began with a single teenage collaborator became trenchant social commentary, overturning the kinds of adventure stories that typically feature boys. As Kurland put it, “I staged the girls as a standing army of teenaged runaways in resistance to patriarchal ideals.”

Danny Lyon

In this scene, Danny Lyon photographs Lower Manhattan as it’s being emptied out—cast-iron facades still upright, streets suddenly wide with absence, demolition debris gathering at the edges. A lone figure crosses the frame as if passing through a city that’s already becoming a memory.

Lyon, who was born in New York, in 1942, is one of the key postwar American documentary photographers. He has consistently been drawn to communities and places under pressure. Here he chronicled the “slum clearance” demanded by vast civic projects like the original World Trade Center, making pictures that feel like both record and eulogy. Aperture’s 2020 facsimile The Destruction of Lower Manhattan returns to Lyon’s original 1969 photobook, bringing its acts of witness before new audiences and reminding us of the downtown architecture this city once had.

Sophie Rivera

In this picture, Sophie Rivera photographs a server front-on, framed tightly against a dark wall so that the crisp bow tie, jacket lapels, and white apron read almost like a costume. The sitter’s expression is steady but hard to place—professional, guarded, a little weary—while the flash fixes them in a moment of work that might otherwise pass unnoticed. Made in New York as Rivera was developing a photography rooted in Nuyorican life, the picture turns everyday labor into a direct encounter. The image sits within a wider body of portraits and street photographs shaped by feminist and political consciousness, insisting that dignity, complexity, and self-definition can begin in ordinary rooms and routines.

Coreen Simpson

Coreen Simpson photographs four young champions as if they were a single unit—lined up shoulder-to-shoulder, knees bent, ready. The jump rope cuts across the frame like a drawn line, tightening the composition further. Matching uniforms and headbands signal pride and discipline, but what really holds your attention is the girls’ attitude: each face meets the camera with a different mix of cool, focus, and challenge.

Simpson made images like this while covering New York’s cultural life from the late 1970s onward, bringing the tools of editorial photography to scenes that mainstream coverage often overlooked. Here, the uniforms and headbands are part of the performance. The picture also captures an important New York continuum—girls’ games and street culture alongside the early hip-hop era’s emphasis on crew, stance, and self-making in public.

Aperture Loves New York is on view at Aperture through November 1, 2026.

"维尼塔·萨尔马、梅纳兹·巴诺和加尔吉·钱多拉可能从未相遇，但她们的作品相互连接并共享空间，为这场对话带来了多元的视角、思想与理念。女性身份从不单一或固定，其表达亦是如此。每一幅草图、每一件构图都承载着多重的故事、神话与生活经验。个体的声音承载着多重的回响。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她是母亲，是歌姬，是女族长", article_text:
Gargi Chandola, Puge, Gouache on Wasli.

She is her Self.

She is memory, and body.

She is also the landscape and forest.

She is soft and strong, loud and quiet, beautiful and grotesque…

She evolves with the consciousness of a thousand women before her, and will pass it on to ten thousand after. She is a mountain of love, concealing and revealing mythologies.

To describe the work “God Empress of Dune” by Gargi Chandola without employing poetic responses would be doing it an injustice. It is a timeless contemporary visualisation that embodies the spirit of countless beings and generations; representing experiences, memories, power and vulnerability, and the identities of women across time and space. For me, it also embodies the lens through which this essay explores the work of three women – Vinita Sharma, Mainaz Bano, and Gargi Chandola – who are working within the visual legacy of miniature painting, sharing a common contemporary. Each of them highlights an innate capacity to poetically bring forth what is personal and private, even while engaging with and shaping collective thought and expression. Through their work, we encounter what they witness, how they understand, define and express, where their lives’ experience is leading them. We are introduced to their visions of their past and present, their dreams for the future. Significantly, we understand how they derive from, and yet break-away and redefine the rules of miniature painting.

The Storyteller

Vinita Sharma has been painting for around three decades. With a natural affinity to art and aesthetics, she was guided by her husband, prominent miniature painter Ajay Kumar Sharma, in the intricacies of miniature painting. While their repertoire includes Pahari, Kangra and other Indian styles, the larger focus is on the Mughal tradition. After her training, as their children grew older, Vinita had more time to spend on painting, and moved between creating experimental compositions, and more traditional ones that were commissioned and in demand.

An early self-portrait titled “Wandering Thoughts” demonstrates her fluid use of the medium, and her comfort with the rules of miniature painting, that she dissolves in order to express something deeply personal. The composition, in soft blues and browns, depicts the protagonist seemingly in a day-dream while her imagination is fed by the many manuscripts and books that are perhaps her learning blocks as an evolving artist.

Vinit Sharma, Untitled, Waterbased colour on Indian Wasli Handmade

When questioned about her favourite element in miniature painting, she replies with great joy that it lies in the rich detailing – she loves the minute and painstakingly developed patterns – on a sword, a dress or carpet; the delicacy of line and the luminosity of colour that complement each other to make a vibrant whole. She explains how intrinsic the natural pigments and time intensive techniques are to the results, and the manner in which she and Ajay Sharma strive to continue the long-standing practices, even when organic materials (like Khadia or alabaster clay) have become scarce and harder to come by. With their expertise, together they teach workshops on miniature painting, invited to universities and museums both in India and abroad.

Geometric design is another fascination for Vinita. Having spent extended time hosting workshops in West Asian nations, she has used her inspiration from Islamic architectural elements and combined it with her knowledge of distinctive Mughal patterns in order to construct compositions that are as playful as they are compositionally balanced. In a current series of paintings on Kabir, she includes the celebration of the festival of Holi, utilising the structures offered by the geometric designs to create intuitive figurative scenarios.

Exploring the sensitive subject of physical distance and longing, another very popular series of works by her picturises the emotional status of every would-be grandparent awaiting the arrival of a grandchild in a far-away land. Expanding into a wider narrative of domestic spaces, she has painted naughty children, disobedient pets, and preoccupied mothers in these tableaus of love, imbuing the portraiture with a distinctive sweetness and producing interesting detailing such as trees filled with patterned motifs rather than leaf forms.

In her work, factual experience finds form in imaginary storytelling and vice versa, and her image-making process moves freely between varied vocabularies of the miniature, uniting the regional and global, and bringing the past and present together in seamless rhythm.

The Chronicler

Resonating with a methodology and visual practice similar to that of Vinita Sharma, Mainaz Bano has developed a unique style that positions her work within the city of Lucknow, where she is based. Surrounded by Indo-Islamic architecture, and the once renowned ‘ganga-jamuni tehzeeb’ a syncretic culture that speaks of the confluence of the rivers as well as people, their language, beliefs and practices – Mainaz has continually absorbed and chronicled elements from this experience. The worlds she paints are inhabited by characters that traverse historical and contemporary narratives, building bridges between personal observations, popular culture and socio-political realities. For her, the past is what makes the present possible and relevant, and therefore research forms a strong part of her process.

In love with painting and drawing from her childhood, Mainaz was drawn to the aesthetics of miniature painting in her school years, at first diligently making copies and later going on to pursue it while earning a Masters degree in creative landscape painting. Though she trained in the use of traditional pigments, she turned to the use of acrylic on canvas as she began to make larger works. Her compositions make lyrical use of space, colour and line, juxtaposing areas of intricate detail with vacant or minimally handled sections within which objects, flora-fauna and figures emerge; she compares this visual arrangement to the pace of life, that needs pauses amidst the chaos in order to understand oneself and move forward in a balanced way.

Gargi Chandola, Treasure Hunt, Gouache on Wasli.

An unusual and ambitious painting in her repertoire is ‘Evolution 2’, wherein she includes her self-portrait, seated at a table with the (in)famous Begum Samru, a catholic convert who started her life as a nautch girl but navigated her circumstances to become a powerful mercenary ruler in the region of Sardhana, in the early nineteenth century. Deeply intrigued by stories of women such as her, Mainaz presents a translated version of an earlier court miniature ‘ Begum Samru and her household’ (circa 1820, Delhi, Chester Beatty Library). The ninety-five animated figures represent historical characters as well as her friends and several others known in Lucknow society. The environment opens out into the distinctive Mughal Charbagh, with the University Library as the backdrop and a modern street in the foreground. Deeply philosophical about the human condition, she employs linear forms as a device to comment on life’s transitions and its incompleteness; she also infuses her scenes with elements of humour, invoking the absurd alongside the solemn.

The Critic or the Learner

Humour and satire also form an essential visual and conceptual layer in Gargi Chandola’s versatile practice. Significant in her recent body of work is a series of miniatures that include the presence of Rhesus Macaques, a species of monkey indigenous to the forested areas of the Aravali mountain range where the artist resides. Sometimes relegated to the richly pigmented borders, and at others paired with the Nayika within a lush landscape, these creatures embody behaviours that offer parallels to human nature, demonstrating greed and desire, aggression and dominance, and the will to survive, among other things.

As seen in works like ‘Treasure Hunt’ and ‘Purge’, the Nayikas appear fully in control of their wants and nonchalantly take charge of their surroundings. While a certain sexual symbolism carries forward the commentary on gender hierarchies and power play, the Nayika’s themselves transcend objectification, representing instead the wisdom and playfulness, the resilience and righteousness of the Woman in plurality. Here is a being who embraces and envelopes the multilayered quality of feminine existence, that Gargi says comes from her own deep relationships with all the women in her extended family.

While being connected to creative making from her childhood, Gargi found her calling as an artist after having trained in the guru-shishya parampara to learn the techniques of Basohli, Pahari and Kangra schools of painting. Deeply interested in the pursuit of traditional art forms, she recently took time to teach herself the challenging technique of Turkish ebru-marbling on paper, a process that she is now experimenting with to represent the rugged rock formations that are so much part of her home environment.

Miniature painting, which may have experienced a low period a decade or two ago, is riding on a good wave now. As Vinita Sharma shares, a lot of artists from the younger generations are investing time and energy in learning these old and trusted techniques, often reframing them to fit within personal contemporary explorations.

Vinita Sharma, Mainaz Bano and Gargi Chandola may have never met, but their works connect and share common space, bringing varied perspectives, thoughts and ideas to this dialogue. Womanhood is never singular or fixed, nor is the expression of it. Every sketch, every composition holds multiple stories, mythologies and lived experiences. The individual voice carries the resonance of multiples.

She is the mother, the nautch girl, the matriarch

The black sheep and the white, the found and the lost,

She encompasses all

She belongs. She is.

editorial_title_zh: 每一次时尚将艺术搬上T台
editorial_excerpt_zh: 从短暂的建筑到行为艺术，2027春夏系列尝试了构建时装秀的全新方式。这是一条穿梭于作品与布景之间的探索之路，旨在理解公众体验如何改变，以及演出的常规究竟受到了多少质疑……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "甚至在服装登场之前，凝视的力量就在T台上演。只需观察头排，便能辨认出出席者与阶层间的地理格局：谁占据中心，谁被拍照，谁在观察，谁又主要是在那里供人观赏。时尚在岁月中将这一仪式臻于完美，将身体的展示与声望的呈现交织在一起。嘉宾的座次安排正是其中的一部分。它确立了距离与归属，甚至在秀开始前就引导了注意力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在2027春夏的时装秀中，多个项目恰恰干预了这种呈现的条件。在芬迪（Fendi），观众在试图辨认运动中的身体时，迎面撞上了自己的倒影；在葆蝶家（Bottega Veneta），他们落座于由一个拥抱的物理压力催生出的雕塑之上。在莫斯奇诺（Moschino），一群日常形象的人潮以相反方向穿过了模特们的路线。在别处，一块巨大的织物指引着舞者的动作，一座图书馆变成了T台。奢侈品体系早已习惯于令人难忘的环境层层升级。然而，这些干预同样参与了对秀后注定要广为流传的影像的竞争。不过，它们的兴味所在，恰恰在于它们在服装与观察者之间建立的关系。其中一些作品清晰地表明，时尚究竟吸收了多少20世纪下半叶艺术中的一个核心议题：一件作品呈现时的条件，正构成了其意义的一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Durazzi-2-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Durazzi", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "1976年，布赖恩·奥多尔蒂（Brian O’Doherty）在《艺术论坛》（Artforum）上发表了后来结集为《白立方体内：现代主义展厅空间的意识形态》（Inside the White Cube）的系列文章，对现代主义展览空间所谓的中立性提出了质疑。白色的墙壁、照明以及与外界的隔离构建了作品的权威，并暗示观众该如何行事。1979年，罗莎琳德·克劳斯（Rosalind Krauss）凭借《扩展场域中的雕塑》（Sculpture in the Expanded Field）审视了雕塑实践的拓展及其与建筑和景观的关系。这些工具即便在面对T台时也同样实用，前提是必须分清展览的目的与时装秀的目的。它们有助于人们认识到，一项建筑学的选择能在多大程度上决定视觉体验。转移观众、打断一条路线或引入一面镜子，都会改变观者的体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "凝视那艰难的天真", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在芬迪的时装秀上，玛丽亚·格拉齐亚·基尤里（Maria Grazia Chiuri）在环境中央放置了一个受到卢西亚诺·法布罗（Luciano Fabro）《镜立方》（Cubo di specchi）启发而创作的镜面体。该参考对象为其《剧场布景：镜立方》（Allestimento teatrale. Cubo di specchi，1967-1975），这是一件通过反射面将观察者引入作品空间的作品。观者还必须面对自身的影像。基尤里将作为贫穷艺术（Arte Povera）核心人物的法布罗的研究，与拉法埃拉·卡拉（Raffaella Carrà）和阿德里亚诺·切连塔诺（Adriano Celentano）的电视视觉形象结合在一起，唤起了那场著名的表演《Prisencolinensinainciusol》。这是艺术实验与意大利流行文化之间一次意料之外的邂逅。倒影与集体运动将诞生于不同语境、拥有各自受众和语言的经验串联在了一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Fendi-1024x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Fendi", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "普拉达（Prada）则通过一种近乎具有分析严谨性的环境来处理视觉。在普拉达基金会（Fondazione Prada）的仓库（Deposito）中，OMA设计了一个由发光元素交织而成的有机玻璃（Perspex）地面，呼应了同一季节早前男装发布会所使用的结构。这种效果让人想起一张巨大的发光桌子，上面的身影仿佛被置于审视之下。由缪奇娜·普拉达（Miuccia Prada）和拉夫·西蒙斯（Raf Simons）共同创作、名为《半身裙》（The Skirt）的系列，将探讨集中于半身裙上，并在限定的参数内对其进行种种变奏。布景呼应了这一选择。结构保持不变，使得服装之间的差异更加清晰易读。观众也被邀请进行一场专注力的练习，去辨认一个看似整齐划一的序列内部究竟发生了什么变化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "我们落座其上的作品", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在葆蝶家（Bottega Veneta），艺术与设计的关系呈现出一种立即可感的形式：嘉宾们坐在艺术品上。对于露易丝·特罗特（Louise Trotter）的2027夏季系列而言，座位是伊利亚·戈尔德曼·古宾（Illya Goldman Gubin）的“纸箱凳”（Karton Hocker），它们由经由一个拥抱而变形的纸箱制成。随后，这种形状被固化并变得持久，将最初那次压力的记忆保留在褶皱与挤压之中。在每个座位上，都有一朵手工制作的皮革花朵。该项目还涉及声音。由弗洛里安·赫克（Florian Hecker）创作的特定场域装置《闪烁20》（Scintillations 20），包含二十个悬挂结构，配有扬声器和不锈钢声学反射器。马克·莱克利（Mark Leckey）是一位实践横跨电影、声音和流行文化的英国艺术家，他为该秀创作了配乐。因此，观众不仅通过视觉，还通过身体接触和听觉置身于一个错综复杂的环境之中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Bottega-Veneta-1-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Bottega Veneta", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相遇的建筑与自由的难题", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《The Atrium Show》中，Durazzi Milano 将这场对话转移到了一个展览内部。该项目由玛尔塔·切雷达（Marta Cereda）、伊lenia·杜拉齐（Ilenia Durazzi）和卡蒂娅·米哈（Katia Miha）构思，在位于罗索利诺·皮洛街（via Rosolino Pilo）的 Atrium 空间内汇集了装置艺术、绘画、雕塑、行为艺术以及档案材料。2027春夏系列《Assemblage》与独立艺术作品共同陈列于此。这种共存使得人们能够通过艺术家们提出的问题来解读服装。在从街头通过三扇大窗户可见的“窗户房”（Windows Room）中，马蒂斯·梅斯尼尔（Matisse Mesnil）展示了《Virale》（2026），这是一组由100个钢制圆锥体组成的装置。这些形态不断重复，构成了一个带有敌意的景观，并让人联想到那些阻止逗留或规范公共空间移动的防御性建筑装置。在同一空间中，卡特琳娜·戈比（Caterina Gobbi）在《La terra ripete la mia voce nella tua》（2026）中将一把电吉他、一个扬声器、鲜花、铁链和玻璃联系在了一起。这件乐器在没有人类表演者的情况下发出声音。在强烈的放大音效之旁，鲜花引入了一种脆弱的、暴露在外的存在。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Durazzi-1-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Durazzi", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "保护与束缚之间的关系在诺娜·因内斯库（Nona Inescu）的贝壳、凝结物和工业结构中再次出现。多娜·瓦雷拉（Dune Varela）则将古代雕塑碎片的照片与大理石并置，让影像的时间与物质的时间相遇。在温室（Serra）中，魔法崇拜（Cult of Magic）的《Fear of the Dark_Open Studio》探讨了视觉方向感的丧失以及想象力在黑暗中所产生的东西。盖亚·吉内芙拉·焦尔吉（Gaia Ginevra Giorgi）的《Ecotongues》则致力于将声音作为人与超人类之间的阈值。由Careof录像档案馆精选的《Happening Fragments, Milan, 1992-2007》中的影像，将米兰独立场景的行动与相遇带回了展览空间。《Assemblage》探讨了通过可拆卸的衣领、袖子和衬里、并置的材料以及模块化结构来修改服装的可能性。衣橱可以被拆解并重新组合。在展览中，这种可变形性与那些质疑强加给身体及其运动的限制的作品展开了对话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "人群、手势、抗拒形式的身体", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "时尚与行为艺术之间的关系有着先例，这有助于我们解读本季的实验。1959年，阿兰·卡普罗（Allan Kaprow）创作了《18 Happenings in 6 Parts》，呼吁观众在限定的时间和空间组织内执行特定的动作。观众的出席及其行为被纳入了活动的构建之中。因此，参与也有其自身的规则。近40年后，亚历山大·麦昆（Alexander McQueen）将这种张力赋予了他最具震撼力的视觉形象之一。在1998年呈献的1999春夏系列《No. 13》的尾声中，沙洛姆·哈洛（Shalom Harlow）在一个平台上旋转，而两台工业机器人将颜料喷洒在她的白色连衣裙上。这一灵感来自丽贝卡·霍恩（Rebecca Horn）装置的行动，在观众面前改造了这件衣服。观众们见证了服装获得其最终形态的时刻，而这一转变将与其形象密不可分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Issey-Miyake-2-1024x683.jpg", "alt": "T台上的艺术", "caption": "三宅一生", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在洛里斯·墨西拿（Loris Messina）和西蒙娜·里佐（Simone Rizzo）担任莫斯奇诺（Moschino）创意总监的首秀上，行为与导演之间的关系通过人群得以展现。在米兰郊区一个多层停车场的屋顶上，数百名临时演员与模特背道而驰，穿过了T台。儿童、自行车、狗以及身着日常服装的身影，给人一种都市人流突然闯入时尚表演场所的印象。街道表面上的混乱感，交由临时演员和一条预设路线去完成，依然是一种导演的选择。三宅一生则将注意力集中在身体与面料之间的距离上。在巴黎柔道馆（Dojo de Paris）呈献的《Figure of Ma》系列以一场由泰斯·福尔克（Tess Voelker）编导的表演开场。11名舞者操纵着一块巨大的蓝色织物。布料升起、落下、留住空气；体积随着每一次运动而改变，所有参与其中的身体都无法单独定义它们。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“间”（Ma），这个日语概念指的是事物之间的间隔或空间，为解读该系列提供了一把钥匙。服装在织物材料与穿着者之间的距离中成形，这种距离在运动中被不断改变。这场表演使这种空间变得清晰可感，而当我们观察一件衣服时，这种空间通常很难被孤立出来。钢琴家中木考树（Koki Nakano）参与了该系列的概念和音乐开发。他的参与将声音带入了对形态的研究之中。音乐和手势共同促成了一种体验，在这种体验中，体积在观众的注视下于时间中得以确立。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "档案、纪念碑与图像：作为布景的记忆", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在巴黎的圣热讷维耶芙图书馆（Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève），亚历山德罗·米开莱（Alessandro Michele）为华伦天奴（Valentino）呈献了《Antibiblioteca》。该系列汲取自纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布（Nassim Nicholas Taleb）通过翁贝托·埃科（Umberto Eco）的个人藏书为例所阐述的概念，其中尚未阅读的书籍表明了仍有多少知识需要去了解。由亨利·拉布鲁斯特（Henri Labrouste）于1838年至1850年间设计的建筑为这一思考提供了一个具体的场所。在大阅览室里，纤细的铸铁柱和金属拱顶将结构展现为建筑语言的一部分。在立面上，810个文化与科学界杰出男士的名字将知识与进步的理念刻在石头上。米开莱在这个环境中引入了关于尚未探索的可能性的主题。该系列文本还呼应了吉尔乔·阿甘本（Giorgio Agamben），将那些永远不会被穿上的服装赋予了让人想象其他生存方式的能力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Valentino-1024x682.jpg", "alt": "T台上的艺术", "caption": "华伦天奴", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "宾客们被要求携带图书捐赠给公共图书馆。这一举动将时装秀的排他性与知识的公众获取联系在了一起。时装秀的排他性与图书馆的公共功能之间的距离依然清晰可见，这也是该项目吸引人的一部分。在圣罗兰（Saint Laurent），记忆则化为一种重建的环境。安东尼·瓦卡莱罗（Anthony Vaccarello）为2027春夏系列将特罗卡代罗（Trocadéro）广场变成了一个由金色和巨型枝形吊灯主导的布景。其参照物是洲际酒店（Hôtel Inter-Continental）的帝王沙龙（Salon Impérial），伊夫·圣罗兰（Yves Saint Laurent）正是在那里于1976年开始发布其高级定制系列。开云集团（Kering）在2026年10月9日发布的官方公告中宣布了瓦卡莱罗在担任十年创意总监后离任的消息，这让人不禁将这一场景解读为一场可能的告别。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从记忆向服装形象的过渡在MSGM身上找到了另一个例证。马西莫·焦尔杰蒂（Massimo Giorgetti）围绕马里奥·斯基法诺（Mario Schifano）的艺术世界展开创作，通过与管理其艺术遗产的基金会达成协议，在设计中融入了星星和心形等母题。“从我开始”（Ricomincio da me）这一与1983年一次采访相关的表述，伴随着品牌身份重新定义的一个时刻。斯基法诺的符号进入了时尚影像的流通中，即便在远离艺术语境的地方遇到它们，也要求人们能够将其认出。这开启了一个不同于展陈所提出的问题：当艺术家的母题成为品牌身份的一部分时，其研究中有多少内容依然清晰可读？一场时装秀可以改变形态，却让自身的层级结构完好无损。当我们面对精美绝伦的布景时，与艺术的相遇唯有在它帮助我们认出这些层级时，才会获得批判的力量。从头排到T台，问题依然悬而未决：我们的目光究竟拥有多少自由，又是谁在继续引导它？", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Prima ancora degli abiti, in passerella va in scena il potere dello sguardo. Basta osservare una prima fila per riconoscere la geografia delle presenze e delle gerarchie: chi occupa il centro, chi viene fotografato, chi guarda e chi è lì soprattutto per essere guardato. La moda ha perfezionato questo rituale nel tempo, intrecciando l’esibizione del corpo alla rappresentazione del prestigio. La disposizione degli ospiti ne è parte. Stabilisce distanze e appartenenze, orienta l’attenzione ancora prima che lo show cominci."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nelle sfilate della Primavera/Estate 2027, diversi progetti intervengono proprio sulle condizioni di questa rappresentazione. Da Fendi, gli spettatori hanno incontrato il proprio riflesso mentre cercavano di distinguere i corpi in movimento; da Bottega Veneta hanno preso posto su sculture nate dalla pressione fisica di un abbraccio. Da Moschino, una folla di figure quotidiane ha attraversato il percorso dei modelli in direzione contraria. Altrove, un grande tessuto ha guidato il movimento dei danzatori e una biblioteca è diventata passerella. Il sistema del lusso ci ha abituati a un’escalation di ambientazioni memorabili. Anche questi interventi partecipano alla competizione per l’immagine destinata a circolare dopo lo show. Il loro interesse, però, sta nel rapporto che costruiscono fra gli abiti e chi li osserva. Alcuni rendono evidente quanto la moda abbia assimilato una questione centrale nell’arte del secondo Novecento: le condizioni in cui un’opera appare contribuiscono al suo significato."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Durazzi-2-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Durazzi", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Nel 1976 Brian O’Doherty pubblicava su Artforum i saggi poi raccolti in Inside the White Cube , mettendo in discussione la presunta neutralità dello spazio espositivo modernista. Il bianco delle pareti, l’illuminazione e l’isolamento dal mondo esterno costruivano l’autorità dell’opera, suggerendo allo spettatore come comportarsi. Nel 1979, con Sculpture in the Expanded Field , Rosalind Krauss avrebbe esaminato l’ampliamento delle pratiche scultoree e le loro relazioni con l’architettura e il paesaggio. Sono strumenti di lettura utili anche davanti a una passerella, purché si mantengano distinte le finalità di una mostra da quelle di una sfilata. Aiutano a riconoscere quanto una scelta architettonica condizioni la visione. Spostare il pubblico, interrompere un percorso o introdurre uno specchio cambia l’esperienza di chi guarda."}, {"type": "heading", "text": "La difficile innocenza dello sguardo"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Alla sfilata Fendi, Maria Grazia Chiuri ha collocato al centro dell’ambiente un volume specchiante ispirato al Cubo di specchi di Luciano Fabro. Il riferimento è ad Allestimento teatrale. Cubo di specchi (1967-1975), un lavoro nel quale la superficie riflettente introduce l’osservatore nello spazio dell’opera. Chi guarda deve fare i conti anche con la propria immagine. Chiuri accosta la ricerca di Fabro, figura centrale dell’Arte Povera, all’immaginario televisivo di Raffaella Carrà e Adriano Celentano, evocando la celebre performance di Prisencolinensinainciusol . È un incontro inatteso fra sperimentazione artistica e cultura popolare italiana. Il riflesso e il movimento collettivo mettono in comunicazione esperienze nate in contesti diversi, con pubblici e linguaggi propri."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Fendi-1024x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Fendi", "credit": "Exibart"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Prada affronta la visione attraverso un ambiente di rigore quasi analitico. article_text:
Prima ancora degli abiti, in passerella va in scena il potere dello sguardo. Basta osservare una prima fila per riconoscere la geografia delle presenze e delle gerarchie: chi occupa il centro, chi viene fotografato, chi guarda e chi è lì soprattutto per essere guardato. La moda ha perfezionato questo rituale nel tempo, intrecciando l’esibizione del corpo alla rappresentazione del prestigio. La disposizione degli ospiti ne è parte. Stabilisce distanze e appartenenze, orienta l’attenzione ancora prima che lo show cominci.

Nelle sfilate della Primavera/Estate 2027, diversi progetti intervengono proprio sulle condizioni di questa rappresentazione. Da Fendi, gli spettatori hanno incontrato il proprio riflesso mentre cercavano di distinguere i corpi in movimento; da Bottega Veneta hanno preso posto su sculture nate dalla pressione fisica di un abbraccio. Da Moschino, una folla di figure quotidiane ha attraversato il percorso dei modelli in direzione contraria. Altrove, un grande tessuto ha guidato il movimento dei danzatori e una biblioteca è diventata passerella. Il sistema del lusso ci ha abituati a un’escalation di ambientazioni memorabili. Anche questi interventi partecipano alla competizione per l’immagine destinata a circolare dopo lo show. Il loro interesse, però, sta nel rapporto che costruiscono fra gli abiti e chi li osserva. Alcuni rendono evidente quanto la moda abbia assimilato una questione centrale nell’arte del secondo Novecento: le condizioni in cui un’opera appare contribuiscono al suo significato.

Nel 1976 Brian O’Doherty pubblicava su Artforum i saggi poi raccolti in Inside the White Cube , mettendo in discussione la presunta neutralità dello spazio espositivo modernista. Il bianco delle pareti, l’illuminazione e l’isolamento dal mondo esterno costruivano l’autorità dell’opera, suggerendo allo spettatore come comportarsi. Nel 1979, con Sculpture in the Expanded Field , Rosalind Krauss avrebbe esaminato l’ampliamento delle pratiche scultoree e le loro relazioni con l’architettura e il paesaggio. Sono strumenti di lettura utili anche davanti a una passerella, purché si mantengano distinte le finalità di una mostra da quelle di una sfilata. Aiutano a riconoscere quanto una scelta architettonica condizioni la visione. Spostare il pubblico, interrompere un percorso o introdurre uno specchio cambia l’esperienza di chi guarda.

La difficile innocenza dello sguardo

Alla sfilata Fendi, Maria Grazia Chiuri ha collocato al centro dell’ambiente un volume specchiante ispirato al Cubo di specchi di Luciano Fabro. Il riferimento è ad Allestimento teatrale. Cubo di specchi (1967-1975), un lavoro nel quale la superficie riflettente introduce l’osservatore nello spazio dell’opera. Chi guarda deve fare i conti anche con la propria immagine. Chiuri accosta la ricerca di Fabro, figura centrale dell’Arte Povera, all’immaginario televisivo di Raffaella Carrà e Adriano Celentano, evocando la celebre performance di Prisencolinensinainciusol . È un incontro inatteso fra sperimentazione artistica e cultura popolare italiana. Il riflesso e il movimento collettivo mettono in comunicazione esperienze nate in contesti diversi, con pubblici e linguaggi propri.

Prada affronta la visione attraverso un ambiente di rigore quasi analitico. Nel Deposito di Fondazione Prada, OMA ha progettato un pavimento in Perspex scandito da elementi luminosi, riprendendo la struttura utilizzata per la precedente presentazione maschile della stessa stagione. L’effetto ricorda un enorme tavolo luminoso, sul quale le figure sembrano offerte all’osservazione. La collezione di Miuccia Prada e Raf Simons, intitolata The Skirt , concentra l’indagine sulla gonna, sottoposta a variazioni entro parametri definiti. L’allestimento accompagna questa scelta. La struttura resta costante e rende più leggibili le differenze fra gli abiti. Anche il pubblico viene invitato a un esercizio di attenzione, a riconoscere ciò che cambia dentro una sequenza apparentemente uniforme.

L’opera sulla quale ci sediamo

Da Bottega Veneta, il rapporto fra arte e design prende una forma immediatamente comprensibile: gli ospiti si siedono sulle opere. Per la Summer 2027 di Louise Trotter, le sedute erano i Karton Hocker di Illya Goldman Gubin, ottenuti da scatole di cartone deformate attraverso un abbraccio. La forma viene poi consolidata e resa durevole, conservando nelle pieghe e nelle compressioni la memoria di quella pressione iniziale. Su ciascuna seduta, un fiore in pelle realizzato a mano. Il progetto coinvolgeva anche il suono. Scintillations 20 , installazione site-specific di Florian Hecker, comprendeva venti strutture sospese dotate di altoparlanti e riflettori acustici in acciaio inossidabile. Mark Leckey, artista britannico la cui pratica attraversa cinema, suono e cultura popolare, ha realizzato la colonna sonora dello show. Il pubblico si trovava dunque dentro un ambiente articolato attraverso il contatto fisico e l’ascolto, oltre che attraverso la visione.

L’architettura dell’incontro e il problema della libertà

Con The Atrium Show , Durazzi Milano sposta il confronto all’interno di una mostra. Il progetto, ideato da Marta Cereda, Ilenia Durazzi e Katia Miha negli ambienti di Atrium, in via Rosolino Pilo, riunisce installazioni, pittura, scultura, performance e materiali d’archivio. La collezione Primavera/Estate 2027, Assemblage , vi trova posto accanto a opere autonome. Questa convivenza permette di leggere gli abiti attraverso le domande sollevate dagli artisti. Nella Windows Room, visibile dalla strada attraverso tre grandi finestre, Matisse Mesnil presenta Virale (2026), un insieme di cento coni d’acciaio. La forma si ripete fino a comporre un paesaggio ostile e richiama i dispositivi dell’architettura difensiva che impediscono la sosta o regolano i movimenti nello spazio pubblico. Nello stesso ambiente, Caterina Gobbi mette in relazione una chitarra elettrica, un amplificatore, fiori, catene e vetro in La terra ripete la mia voce nella tua (2026). Lo strumento suona senza un esecutore umano. Accanto alla forza del suono amplificato, i fiori introducono una presenza fragile, esposta.

Il rapporto fra protezione e costrizione torna nelle conchiglie, nelle concrezioni e nelle strutture industriali di Nona Inescu. Dune Varela accosta, invece, fotografie di frammenti scultorei antichi al marmo, facendo incontrare il tempo dell’immagine con quello della materia. Nella Serra, Fear of the Dark_Open Studio di Cult of Magic esplora la perdita dell’orientamento visivo e ciò che l’immaginazione produce nell’oscurità. Ecotongues di Gaia Ginevra Giorgi lavora sulla voce come soglia fra umano e più-che-umano. Le immagini di Happening Fragments, Milan, 1992-2007 , selezionate dal Careof Video Archive, riportano nello spazio espositivo azioni e incontri della scena indipendente milanese. Assemblage affronta la possibilità di modificare l’abito attraverso colli, maniche e fodere removibili, materiali accostati e costruzioni modulari. Il guardaroba può essere smontato e ricomposto. Nella mostra, questa trasformabilità entra in dialogo con opere che interrogano i limiti imposti al corpo e ai suoi movimenti.

La folla, il gesto, il corpo che resiste alla forma

La relazione fra moda e performance ha precedenti che aiutano a leggere gli esperimenti di questa stagione. Nel 1959 Allan Kaprow realizzava 18 Happenings in 6 Parts , chiamando il pubblico a compiere azioni specifiche dentro un’organizzazione temporale e spaziale definita. La presenza degli spettatori e i loro comportamenti entravano nella costruzione dell’evento. Anche la partecipazione, dunque, aveva le proprie regole. Quasi quarant’anni dopo, Alexander McQueen avrebbe dato a questa tensione una delle sue immagini più potenti. Nel finale di No. 13 , collezione Primavera/Estate 1999 presentata nel 1998, Shalom Harlow ruotava su una piattaforma mentre due robot industriali spruzzavano vernice sul suo abito bianco. L’azione, ispirata a un’installazione di Rebecca Horn, trasformava il vestito davanti al pubblico. Gli spettatori assistevano al momento in cui l’abito acquisiva la propria forma finale, e quella trasformazione sarebbe rimasta inseparabile dalla sua immagine.

Al debutto di Loris Messina e Simone Rizzo alla direzione creativa di Moschino, il rapporto fra comportamento e regia passa attraverso una folla. Sul tetto di un parcheggio multipiano alla periferia di Milano, centinaia di comparse hanno attraversato la passerella in senso contrario ai modelli. Bambini, biciclette, cani e figure in abiti quotidiani davano l’impressione di un flusso urbano entrato improvvisamente nel luogo della rappresentazione moda. Il disordine apparente della strada, affidato a comparse e a un percorso prestabilito, rimaneva una scelta di regia. Issey Miyake concentra invece l’attenzione sulla distanza fra il corpo e il tessuto. La collezione Figure of Ma , presentata al Dojo de Paris, si è aperta con una performance coreografata da Tess Voelker. Undici danzatori hanno manipolato un grande tessuto azzurro. La stoffa si sollevava, ricadeva, tratteneva l’aria; i volumi cambiavano a ogni movimento e nessuno dei corpi coinvolti poteva definirli da solo.

Il ma , concetto giapponese che indica l’intervallo o lo spazio fra le cose, offre una chiave per leggere la collezione. L’abito prende forma nella distanza fra la materia tessile e chi la indossa, una distanza che il movimento continua a modificare. La performance rende percepibile questo spazio, normalmente difficile da isolare quando osserviamo un vestito. Il pianista Koki Nakano ha partecipato allo sviluppo concettuale e musicale della collezione. Il suo coinvolgimento porta il suono dentro la ricerca sulla forma. Musica e gesto concorrono a un’esperienza nella quale i volumi si definiscono nel tempo, sotto gli occhi del pubblico.

Archivi, monumenti e immagini: la memoria come scenografia

Alla Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève di Parigi, Alessandro Michele ha presentato per Valentino Antibiblioteca . La collezione prende avvio dal concetto formulato da Nassim Nicholas Taleb attraverso l’esempio della biblioteca personale di Umberto Eco, dove i libri ancora da leggere indicano quanto resta da conoscere. L’edificio progettato da Henri Labrouste fra il 1838 e il 1850 dà a questa riflessione un luogo preciso. Nella grande sala di lettura, le sottili colonne di ghisa e le volte metalliche mostrano la struttura come parte del linguaggio architettonico. Sulla facciata, 810 nomi di uomini illustri della cultura e della scienza fissano in pietra un’idea di sapere e di progresso. Michele introduce in questo ambiente il tema delle possibilità ancora inesplorate. Il testo della collezione, richiamando anche Giorgio Agamben, attribuisce agli abiti che non saranno mai indossati la capacità di far immaginare altre esistenze.

Agli ospiti è stato chiesto di portare libri da destinare alle biblioteche pubbliche. Il gesto mette in relazione l’esclusività della sfilata con l’accesso collettivo al sapere. La distanza fra l’esclusività della sfilata e la funzione pubblica della biblioteca rimane visibile, ed è parte dell’interesse del progetto. Da Saint Laurent, la memoria prende la forma di un ambiente ricostruito. Per la Primavera/Estate 2027, Anthony Vaccarello ha trasformato l’esplanade del Trocadéro in una scenografia dominata dall’oro e da grandi lampadari. Il riferimento era il Salon Impérial dell’Hôtel Inter-Continental, dove Yves Saint Laurent iniziò a presentare le proprie collezioni haute couture nel 1976. L’annuncio del 9 ottobre 2026, con cui Kering ha ufficializzato l’uscita di Vaccarello dopo dieci anni alla direzione creativa, invita a rileggere quella scena come un possibile commiato.

Il passaggio dalla memoria all’immagine dell’abito trova un altro esempio in MSGM. Massimo Giorgetti ha lavorato sull’universo di Mario Schifano, riprendendone motivi come stelle e cuori attraverso un accordo con la fondazione che ne gestisce l’eredità artistica. Il riferimento a Ricomincio da me , espressione legata a un’intervista del 1983, accompagna un momento di ridefinizione dell’identità del marchio. I segni di Schifano entrano nella circolazione delle immagini di moda, chiedendo di essere riconosciuti anche da chi li incontra lontano dal contesto artistico. Si apre una questione diversa da quella posta dagli allestimenti: quanto della ricerca di un artista rimane leggibile quando i suoi motivi diventano parte dell’identità di un marchio? Una sfilata può cambiare forma e lasciare intatte le proprie gerarchie. L’incontro con l’arte acquista forza critica quando ci aiuta a riconoscerle, anche dentro la meraviglia di un allestimento. Dalla prima fila alla passerella, la domanda resta aperta: quanta libertà ha il nostro sguardo, e chi continua a orientarlo?

"translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "夏洛特姑娘是阿尔弗雷德·丁尼生一首诗的主题，该诗大致取材于阿斯托尔特的伊莲恩（Elaine of Astolat），一个因失恋而死的中世纪亚瑟王传奇人物。丁尼生写过两个版本，分别于1832年和1842年出版，两版有数节不同。我自己是通过洛雷娜·麦肯尼特（Loreena McKennitt）的演绎结识《夏洛特姑娘》这个故事的，她将这首诗谱成了音乐。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丁尼生的夏洛特姑娘居住在流向卡米洛特（Camelot）河中小岛上的一座城堡里。我们无从得知原因，但这位妙龄女子身上诅咒缠身。她不得将目光投向窗外的外部世界，更不用说离开城堡了。她只能通过镜中的反射来观察世界——丁尼生称之为世界的阴影。她必须日夜纺织在镜中映出的场景。她对此并不觉得苦恼：in her web she still delights（她依然沉醉于自己的织网之中）。她稳步地制作着对世界副本的副本。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Spiegelbeelden-afb-1-1171x1600.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "约翰·威廉·沃特豪斯（John William Waterhouse）——《“我厌倦了阴影，”夏洛特姑娘说》，1915年。安大略美术馆，多伦多。来源：维基媒体。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，某种情绪开始啃噬她的内心：‘I am half sick of shadows,’ said / The Lady of Shalott（“我厌倦了阴影，”/ 夏洛特姑娘说）。一天，她在镜中看到威风凛凛的兰斯洛特爵士（Sir Lancelot）策马驶过——或者确切地说，她看到的是他在水中倒影的映射，这是一次双重反射，使她得以不带镜像地看到他。她离开织机，走到窗前向外望去，望向真实的世界。灾难瞬间降临：Out flew the web and floated wide; / The mirror crack’d from side to side; / ‘The curse is come upon me,’ cried / The Lady of Shalott（织网飞出，飘向远方；/ 镜子自此裂为两半；/ “诅咒落在了我身上，”/ 夏洛特姑娘大喊）。这位妙龄女子走到户外，来到河岸，那里停着一艘小船。在船头写上自己的名字后，她躺进船里，任由小船顺流而下驶向卡米洛特，同时唱着她的绝命歌。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Spiegelbeelden-afb-2-941x1600.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "约翰·威廉·沃特豪斯（John William Waterhouse）——《夏洛特姑娘望着兰斯洛特》，1894年。利兹美术馆。来源：维基媒体。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为什么要遭受如此残酷的命运？她究竟做错了什么而招致这个诅咒，为什么她决定——可以说是停止刷手机并参与真实生活——的决定会受到惩罚？为什么她现在又必须为了一个男人而死？丁尼生是一个厌女者吗？他只允许他的女主角扮演被动角色，让她作为一具美丽的死尸顺流漂过，为男人的生活平添一抹神秘色彩？或者他其实是在探讨他那个时代针对女性的贞洁风俗，而诅咒代表着父权制？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了关于骑士与失恋的中世纪故事外，丁尼生的诗中也回荡着古典传统。被囚禁的妙龄女子只能看到世界的阴影，这让人直接联想起柏拉图的洞穴比喻——苏格拉底借此在《理想国》中解释道，感官世界仅仅是永恒理念世界的不完美复制品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "苏格拉底说，想象有一群囚徒被绑在洞穴里，背对洞口，双眼盯着洞穴的后壁。他们身后燃着一堆火，因此囚徒们能在墙上看到洞外发生之事的阴影，同时听到外面声音的回音。因为他们一无所知，所以认为自己感知到的就是真实的世界。囚徒们可以挣脱束缚、转过身去进入真实的世界，但这却是一个痛苦的过程，因为他们的四肢已经痉挛，起初还会被强光刺得眼花缭乱。同样，想要认识多变世界背后真实理念的哲学家之路，也只属于那些坚韧不拔的灵魂。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Spiegelbeelden-afb-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "扬·萨恩雷丹（Jan Saenredam）仿自科内利斯·范·哈勒姆（Cornelis van Haarlem）——《柏拉图的洞穴比喻》，1604年。大英博物馆，伦敦。来源：维基媒体。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管与柏拉图洞穴的对比显而易见，但这并没有让夏洛特姑娘的命运变得更容易理解。如果我们把她看作洞穴中的囚徒之一，那么她背弃镜子、注视真实世界的决定本该受到奖励而不是惩罚。或者说，丁尼生是在赞扬她的毅力——尽管身受诅咒，她依然如此坚定，决定逃离她的阴影世界？我们或许也应该以寓言的方式解读这位妙龄女子的死，将其视为对尘世的一种净化？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，夏洛特姑娘远不止是一个影子旁观者。她还用自己的织机创造图像。丁尼生的这首诗常被解读为关于在孤立中创作的艺术家的寓言，尤其是关于诗歌的寓言——诗歌据称发自内心，而非源自对外部事物的认知。顺便一提，诗中并未交代夏洛特姑娘究竟织了哪些场景，她究竟是忠实复制了镜中影像，还是加入了个人诠释，也无从得知。丁尼生只提到镜中浮现出的葬礼和新婚夫妇，并讲述这位女织工使用了明亮的色彩。在她死后，她的作品又遭遇了什么？丁尼生写道：Out flew the web and floated wide（织物飞出，随风飘荡）。我们可以将其解读为一种爆发式的自我毁灭，但也可以视为织物找到了通往外部世界道路的迹象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "柏拉图对艺术（作为不完美感官世界的一部分）的态度是矛盾的。其中一个核心概念是 mimesis，即模仿。柏拉图认为，仅模仿现实外部特征的艺术是肤浅且幼稚的。然而，具备实用价值的物体的完整复制品（例如手稿的复本）可能有其价值。如果艺术家能通过钻研数学原理或传达更深奥的智慧来参透更深层次的事物，那就更好了。在最高层面上运作的是哲学家兼艺术家，他们已经超脱于感官世界并掌握了理念世界的知识。这位艺术家不仅模仿善良或美好的事物，还能基于这些事物洞察什么是“善”与“美”。艺术必须宣扬这些理想并因而具有乌托邦色彩，以引导观者走向理念。然而，艺术正如试图模仿理念世界的尘世国家一样，永远是不完美的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "柏拉图关于艺术的观点很难契合我们的时代。在他的理想国中，艺术由哲学家领导的国家委员会进行评审和修改——因此审查制度是一种常态。或许更具争议的是柏拉图对物质、感官性以及变幻无常的现实世界的低看。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对柏拉图灵肉分离观念的抵制，构成了艺术家劳拉·埃姆斯利（Laura Emsley）作品的重要部分，而洞穴在她的作品中处于核心地位。根据柏拉图的寓言，内部和外部是截然分开的。但在埃姆斯利看来，洞穴恰恰是二者交汇并融为一体的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "埃姆斯利的作品 CAVE（1997）是一座由一百本理论和哲学书籍的纸浆制成的步入式洞穴，它源于将理论与艺术结合的渴望。在 cave model（2022）中，她则使用印有柏拉图文本的书籍纸浆来制作酷似大脑的雕塑。为了寻找灵感，埃姆斯利回溯时间，越过了柏拉图，去往史前时期，将洞穴壁视为潜意识的投影幕布。对她而言，洞穴并非逃离之所，而是我们应当沉浸其中以寻找自我的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "借由夏洛特姑娘在镜中所见的世间阴影，丁尼生影射了柏拉图的洞穴以及一个由男性主导的哲学传统。但他也将自己的角色置于另一个自古以来便与女性联系在一起的传统中：织造。正如包豪斯艺术家、被誉为纺织艺术教母的安妮·阿尔伯斯（Anni Albers）在其著作 On Weaving（1965）中所写的那样，这种艺术形式堪称艺术史的源头：“Along with cave paintings, threads were among the earliest transmitters of meaning（伴随着洞穴壁画，线绳是最早的意义传播者之一）。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丁尼生显然对织造艺术有着扎实的了解。女主人公凝视的镜子不仅是一个叙事元素：由于织工在工作时面对的是织物的背面，因此他们会借助一面镜子来随时掌握正面呈现出的效果。夏洛特姑娘在镜中看到倒立的镜像这一事实，恰恰有助于她织出一幅未经镜像翻转的真实世界图像。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在经典神话中，女性经常通过织造来掌控自己的命运。她们用图像而非文字来讲述自己的故事（《没有言语只有线》——这是鹿特丹世界博物馆关于刺绣展览的一个绝妙标题）。菲罗墨拉（Philomela）也是如此，她被自己的连襟特透斯（Tereus）强暴——在某些版本中，地点发生在一个洞穴里。随后，特透斯将她囚禁并割掉她的舌头，使她无法向任何人吐露发生过的事。通过将罪行织进挂毯并托人带给一位老妇人，菲罗墨拉成功向前来秘密解救她的妹妹澄清了真相。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Philomela_by_E.C.Burne-Jones_1864_Christies.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "爱德华·伯恩-琼斯（Edward Burne-Jones）——《菲罗墨拉》（Philomela），1864。巴勒莫布特拉宫。图片来源：维基百科。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个故事有过许多重述，但很少被艺术家具象化呈现。其中一个展现了菲罗墨拉作品的例外，是爱德华·伯恩-琼斯（Edward Burne-Jones）于1863年为一幅从未付诸实施的挂毯所作的设计稿。他以乔叟对该故事的十四世纪版本为出发点。菲罗墨拉直立着，手指自己的嘴，以强调她无法言说。她头上方的一卷空白文本再次暗示了她缺乏言语。她手中握着挂毯，上面通过不同场景讲述了她的故事。我们看不到强暴本身，但能看到特透斯将她囚禁。她的织物是一件精致小巧的作品，而乔叟则讲述菲罗墨拉制作了一幅巨大的织物并使用了粗糙的材料——对他而言，强暴的场景并不需要是一个舒适、美观的对象。对于能够通过描绘自己的故事而逃脱的菲罗墨拉来说，织造的作用似乎与夏洛特姑娘的命运截然相反；夏洛特姑娘只能描绘她视线之外的世界，而她的逃离则导致了死亡之果的降临。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "描绘过夏洛特仕女的艺术家们，往往将她的织作置于核心。约翰·威廉·沃特豪斯曾三次将其画入笔下。在他创作于1915年的最后一件作品、题为《“我已厌倦了阴影，”夏洛特仕女说》（‘I am half sick of shadows,’ said the Lady of Shalott）中，我们看到她向后倚靠着坐在织布机前。我们直接望入镜中，镜子里既映射出她自己的作品，也映射出带有卡米洛特的风景。这就像是观者身处现实世界，正透过窗户向内张望，只不过我们在镜中看不到自己。沃特豪斯创作于1894年的第二幅作品也达到了类似的效果。在这里，故事推进得更远了：这位仕女已转过身不再面向织布机，而是正透过窗户凝视——看着我们。她已经被线缠住了，这些线裹在她的双腿周围。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image-1600x1228.jpeg", "alt": "", "caption": "约翰·威廉·沃特豪斯（John William Waterhouse）——《夏洛特仕女》（The Lady of Shalott），1888年。泰特不列颠美术馆，伦敦。来源：维基媒体。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "最为人所知的是沃特豪斯于1888年创作的第一版。这幅画现藏于泰特不列颠美术馆，据说也是该馆最畅销的明信片。在这里，故事又向前推进了一步。夏洛特仕女坐在她的船里，依然挺直着身子，就在她临终前不久。这位仕女带上了她的织物，犹如一件寿衣，又或是留给现实世界的遗产。沃特豪斯显然并不认为诅咒会毁灭这件作品，而是认为它助其走向了世界。当人们发现这块织有场景的布料时——上面甚至可能描绘着他们自己——会作何感想？是一位艺术家、一个抄写员，还是一个偷窥狂？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "观看世界中经媒介中介的影像时所带有的偷窥癖，在当代艺术家埃林·M·莱利（Erin M. Riley）的织毯中扮演着重要角色。她织入的是Pornhub上的截图、随处散落的智能手机以及让人联想起自拍的私密自画像。她通过谷歌、脸书（Facebook）、Instagram和Tumblr搜寻图像。这些织毯呼吁出她成长并塑造了其性观念的聊天室，但通过编织，她同时也背离了数字世界。“我所织出的图像被以一种令人发狂的速度消费并划过，然而织毯却保持着缓慢，”莱利说道。这种偷窥癖既体现在她对在线观察的其他人的使用上，也体现在对她自身身体的描绘中，这把公众变成了偷窥者。如果我们把夏洛特仕女看作一个偷窥狂——一个厚颜无耻地将他人影像用于艺术创作的人——那么在她的故事结尾，我们便会看到一种反转：她冰冷的尸体变成了一场奇观。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.mistermotley.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Spiegelbeelden-afb-6.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "埃林·M·莱利（Erin M. Riley）——《辅助轮》（Training Wheels），2024年。", "credit": "Mister Motley", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丁尼生的两个版本诗作结局各不相同。在1842年的结尾中，人群聚集在仕女的尸体周围。卡米洛特的骑士们满心惊恐地画着十字。只有一位骑士对这番景象并不畏惧：But Lancelot mused a little space; / He said, ‘She has a lovely face; / God in his mercy lend her grace, / The Lady of Shalott.’我更偏爱1832年的结局。在那里，人群同样聚集在尸体周围。人们在仕女的胸口发现了一小片写过字的羊皮纸：‘The web was woven curiously, / The charm is broken utterly, / Draw near and fear not,—this is I, / The Lady of Shalott.’在这里，她至少自己拥有了最后的发言权。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我仍然很想知道的，是这位仕女当时究竟织了什么，她给世界留下了怎样的作品，以及它对人们产生了怎样的影响。我们真的能确凿地说，她在看到镜中的影像之后才将其复制、并重现了现实世界吗？会不会情况恰好相反，是丁尼生全弄错了，她所织出的是一个随后通过镜子向外投射的世界？那将使她成为柏拉图式的造物主（德穆革，demiurge，字面意思是工匠），即那个按照理念世界的模样，用无序的物质塑造出包含神明、行星和人类在内的宇宙的构建者或创造者。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我不认为这个诅咒的目的在于阻止夏洛特仕女去观看真实世界，恰恰相反：它是为了防止人们看到她——活生生的、未经媒介中介的她，不是作为镜像、阴影、故事或织成的艺术品，而是作为创造者。作为一名艺术家，她无论如何都是其作品的创造者，正如所有艺术一样，那件作品也是她所想表达之物的不完美复制品。一旦她停止编织，她也就同时消解了自身，因为创造者唯有在创造的行为中方才存在。艺术家与艺术品无法共存于同一个世界；作为造物主，艺术家属于另一种现实。如果她想把作品送往世界，她自己就必须退场。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此后，人们便只能通过艺术家的形象与相似物——即艺术品——来认识她了。一旦它飞向世界，它便不再仅仅是世界或她内心世界的复制品，而是成为了世界之网的一部分，从而唤起新的阴影与反射。对于这一点，艺术家已然失去了控制权，因为她作为创造者的角色已经谢幕。或许，夏洛特仕女唯有一死，她的作品方能真正活过来。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Lieke Smits onderzoekt in dit essay verschillende draden: spiegelingen, schaduwen, weefwerk, de mogelijkheid om je eigen verhaal te schrijven. Aan de hand van een gedicht van Alfred Tennyson getiteld The Lady of Shalott verkent Lieke wat gezien kan worden als de werkelijkheid en wie verantwoordelijkheid draagt voor hoe we deze zien. ‘Naast middeleeuwse verhalen over ridders en liefdesverdriet, klinken er ook klassieke tradities door in Tennysons gedicht. De opgesloten jonkvrouw die enkel schaduwen van de wereld ziet doet direct denken aan Plato’s allegorie van de grot, waarmee Socrates in De staat uitlegt dat de zintuiglijke wereld slechts een onvolmaakte kopie is van de eeuwige Ideeënwereld’, maar, vervolgt ze ‘De Lady of Shalott is echter meer dan een passieve toeschouwer van schaduwen. Met haar weefgetouw creëert ze ook beelden.’

Er is een vraag die me al zo’n vijfentwintig jaar bezighoudt: waarom moest de Lady of Shalott sterven?

De Lady of Shalott is het onderwerp van een gedicht van Alfred Tennyson, losjes gebaseerd op Elaine van Astolat, een middeleeuws Arthuriaans personage dat overlijdt aan liefdesverdriet. Tennyson schreef twee versies, gepubliceerd in 1832 en 1842, die enkele strofen van elkaar verschillen. Zelf heb ik het verhaal van de Lady of Shalott leren kennen in de uitvoering van Loreena McKennitt, die het gedicht op muziek zette.

Tennysons Lady of Shalott bewoont een kasteel op een eilandje in een rivier die naar Camelot stroomt. Wat de reden ervoor is komen we niet te weten, maar er rust een vloek op de jonkvrouw. Ze mag haar blik niet door het venster op de buitenwereld richten, laat staan haar kasteel verlaten. Ze ziet de wereld enkel via reflecties in haar spiegel – schaduwen van de wereld, noemt Tennyson ze. De scènes die ze weerspiegeld ziet moet ze weven, dag en nacht. Erg vindt ze dat niet: in her web she still delights . Gestaag maakt ze haar kopieën van kopieën van de wereld.

Maar toch begint er iets te knagen: ‘ I am half sick of shadows,’ said / The Lady of Shalott . Op een dag ziet ze in de spiegel de indrukwekkende Sir Lancelot voorbijrijden – of eigenlijk ziet ze de weerspiegeling van zijn reflectie in het water, een dubbele spiegeling waardoor ze hem ongespiegeld ziet. Ze verlaat haar weefgetouw om door het venster naar buiten te kijken, naar de echte wereld. Direct gaat het mis: Out flew the web and floated wide; / The mirror crack’d from side to side; / ‘The curse is come upon me,’ cried / The Lady of Shalott . De jonkvrouw gaat naar buiten, naar de oever waar een boot klaarligt. Op de boeg schrijft ze haar naam, alvorens in de boot te gaan liggen en zich met de stroom mee te laten drijven richting Camelot, terwijl ze haar doodslied zingt.

Waarom dit wrede lot? Waaraan heeft ze die vloek verdiend, waarom wordt ze gestraft voor haar beslissing om bij wijze van spreken te stoppen met scrollen en deel te nemen aan het echte leven? En waarom moet ze nu weer sterven voor een man? Was Tennyson een misogynist die zijn jonkvrouw slechts een passieve rol toestaat, een mooie dode vrouw die langs komt drijven om de levens van mannen van een zweem mysterie te voorzien? Of stelt hij de kuise mores voor vrouwen in zijn tijd juist ter discussie en staat de vloek voor het patriarchaat?

Naast middeleeuwse verhalen over ridders en liefdesverdriet, klinken er ook klassieke tradities door in Tennysons gedicht. De opgesloten jonkvrouw die enkel schaduwen van de wereld ziet doet direct denken aan Plato’s allegorie van de grot, waarmee Socrates in De staat uitlegt dat de zintuiglijke wereld slechts een onvolmaakte kopie is van de eeuwige Ideeënwereld.

Stel je een groep gevangen voor, zegt Socrates, die vastgebonden in een grot zitten, hun rug naar de ingang en hun ogen op de achterwand van de grot gericht. Achter hen brandt een vuur, waardoor de gevangenen op de wand schaduwen zien van wat er buiten de grot gebeurt terwijl ze echo’s van de geluiden van buiten horen. Omdat ze niets anders kennen, denken ze dat ze de echte wereld waarnemen. De gevangenen kunnen zich losmaken, omdraaien en de echte wereld betreden, maar het is een pijnlijk proces, omdat hun ledematen verkrampt zijn en ze aanvankelijk verblind zullen worden door het felle licht. Zo is ook het pad van de filosoof, die de echte Ideeën achter de vergankelijke wereld wil leren kennen, enkel weggelegd voor volhardende zielen.

Hoewel een vergelijking met Plato’s grot voor de hand ligt, maakt die het lot van de Lady of Shalott niet direct begrijpelijker. Als we haar als een van de gevangenen in de grot zien, zou haar beslissing om zich van de spiegel af te wenden en naar de echte wereld te kijken eerder beloond dan bestraft moeten worden. Of prijst Tennyson haar doorzettingsvermogen, dat zo groot is dat ze ondanks de vloek uit haar schaduwrijk besluit te ontsnappen? Moeten we de dood van de jonkvrouw misschien ook allegorisch lezen, als een zuivering van het aardse?

De Lady of Shalott is echter meer dan een passieve toeschouwer van schaduwen. Met haar weefgetouw creëert ze ook beelden. Tennysons gedicht is vaak geïnterpreteerd als een allegorie op de kunstenaar die in isolement werkt, en specifiek op de dichtkunst, die uit het innerlijk zou voortkomen, niet uit kennis van uiterlijke dingen. Welke scènes de Lady of Shalott allemaal weeft komen we in het gedicht overigens niet te weten, of ze de spiegelbeelden trouw kopieert of eigen interpretaties toevoegt ook niet. Tennyson noemt enkel een begrafenis en een bruidspaar die in de spiegel verschijnen en vertelt dat de weefster heldere kleuren gebruikt. En wat gebeurt er na haar dood met het werk? Out flew the web and floated wide , schrijft Tennyson. We kunnen dit lezen als explosieve zelfvernietiging, maar ook als een aanwijzing dat het weefsel een weg naar buiten vindt, de wereld in.

Plato’s houding tegenover kunst, onderdeel van de onvolmaakte zintuiglijke wereld, is ambivalent. Een centraal begrip is daarbij mimesis, nabootsing. Kunst die enkel de uiterlijke kenmerken van de werkelijkheid nabootst noemt Plato oppervlakkig en kinderlijk. Een volledige replica van een object dat praktisch nut heeft, bijvoorbeeld een kopie van een manuscript, kan echter waarde hebben. Nog beter is het wanneer een kunstenaar tot iets diepers weet door te dringen door zich bijvoorbeeld in wiskundige principes te verdiepen of diepere wijsheden over te brengen. Op het allerhoogste niveau opereert de filosoof-kunstenaar, die boven de zintuiglijke wereld is uitgestegen en kennis heeft genomen van de Ideeënwereld. Deze kunstenaar imiteert niet slechts goede of mooie dingen, maar weet op basis van die dingen inzicht te verwerven in wat Goed en Mooi is. Kunst moet deze idealen uitdragen en dus utopisch zijn, om de beschouwer naar de Ideeën te leiden. Toch blijft kunst, net als de aardse staat die de Ideeënwereld probeert te imiteren, altijd onvolmaakt.

Plato’s ideeën over kunst passen moeilijk in onze tijd. In zijn ideale staat wordt kunst in door filosofen geleide staatscommissies beoordeeld en bewerkt – censuur is dus een gangbare praktijk. Wellicht nog bezwaarlijker is Plato’s lage dunk van materie, zintuiglijkheid en de vergankelijke wereld.

Weerstand tegen Plato’s scheiding van geest en materie is een belangrijk onderdeel van het werk van kunstenaar Laura Emsley, waarin grotten centraal staan. Volgens Plato’s allegorie zijn binnenkant en buitenkant gescheiden. Voor Emsley is de grot juist de plaats waar die elkaar raken en met elkaar versmelten.

Emsleys werk CAVE (1997), een inloopgrot gemaakt van het pulp van honderd boeken over theorie en filosofie, kwam voort uit een verlangen om theorie en kunst te verenigen. In cave model (2022) gebruikt ze pulp van boeken met Plato’s teksten om sculpturen te maken die op breinen lijken. Voor haar inspiratie gaat Emsley terug in de tijd, reikt verder dan Plato, naar de prehistorie, met de grotwand als een projectiescherm voor het onbewuste. De grot is voor haar geen plek om uit te ontsnappen, maar een waar we ons in moeten onderdompelen, op zoek naar onszelf.

Met de schaduwen van de wereld die de Lady of Shalott in haar spiegel ziet alludeert Tennyson op Plato’s grot en een door mannen gedomineerde filosofische traditie. Maar hij plaatst zijn personage ook in een andere traditie, die al sinds de Oudheid met vrouwen wordt geassocieerd: die van het weven. Zoals Anni Albers – een Bauhaus-kunstenaar die als de godmother van de textielkunst wordt gezien – in haar boek On Weaving (1965) schreef, stond deze kunstvorm aan de oorsprong van de kunstgeschiedenis: ‘Along with cave paintings, threads were among the earliest transmitters of meaning’.

Tennyson had duidelijk gedegen kennis van de weefkunst. De spiegel waar de jonkvrouw naar kijkt is niet enkel een narratief element: omdat wevers met de achterkant van het doek naar zich toe werken, gebruiken ze een spiegel om de in gaten te houden hoe de voorkant eruit zal komen te zien. Het feit dat de Lady of Shalott de wereld in spiegelbeeld ziet, helpt haar dus om een niet-gespiegelde weergave van de werkelijkheid te weven.

In klassieke mythen zetten vrouwen hun weefwerk regelmatig in om hun eigen lot te sturen. Ze vertellen hun verhalen niet in tekst maar in beeld ( Geen woorden maar draden , was de briljante titel van een tentoonstelling over borduurwerk in het Wereldmuseum Rotterdam). Zo ook Philomela, die verkracht wordt door haar schoonbroer Tereus – in sommige versies in een grot. Vervolgens sluit hij haar op en snijdt haar tong af zodat ze niemand kan vertellen wat er is voorgevallen. Door de misdaad te weven en het tapijt aan een oude vrouw mee te geven, weet Philomela toch duidelijk te maken wat er is gebeurd aan haar zus, die haar heimelijk komt bevrijden.

Het verhaal kent vele hervertellingen, maar is zelden door kunstenaars verbeeld. Een uitzondering, waarop ook Philomela’s werk te zien is, is een ontwerp voor een nooit uitgevoerd tapijt door Edward Burne-Jones uit 1863. Hij nam Chaucers veertiende-eeuwse versie van het verhaal als uitgangspunt. Philomela staat rechtop, wijzend naar haar mond om haar onvermogen tot praten te benadrukken. Een lege tekstrol boven haar hoofd wijst nogmaals op haar gebrek aan woorden. In haar handen houdt ze het tapijt, dat in verschillende scènes haar verhaal uit de doeken doet. De verkrachting zelf zien we niet, wel hoe Tereus haar opsluit. Haar doek is een delicaat, klein werk, terwijl Chaucer vertelt dat Philomela een groot doek maakte en grove materialen noemt – haar verkrachtingsscène hoeft bij hem geen behaaglijk, esthetisch object te zijn. De functie van het weven lijkt voor Philomela, die kan ontsnappen door haar eigen verhaal af te beelden, tegenovergesteld aan het lot van de Lady of Shalott, die enkel de wereld buiten haar zicht mag afbeelden en wier ontsnapping de dood tot gevolg heeft.

Kunstenaars die de Lady of Shalott hebben afgebeeld, stellen haar weefwerk vaak centraal. John William Waterhouse schilderde haar drie keer. In zijn laatste versie, uit 1915, getiteld ‘I am half sick of shadows,’ said the Lady of Shalott , zien we haar achterovergeleund voor haar weefgetouw zitten. We kijken direct in de spiegel, waarin zowel haar eigen werk als een landschap met Camelot is gereflecteerd. Het is alsof de toeschouwer in de buitenwereld is en door het raam naar binnen kijkt, behalve dat we onszelf niet in de spiegel terugzien. Een vergelijkbaar effect wordt bereikt in Waterhouses tweede versie, uit 1894. Hier zijn we verder in het verhaal: de jonkvrouw heeft zich van haar weefgetouw afgewend en kijkt door het venster – naar ons. Ze is verstrikt geraakt in de draden, die om haar benen gewikkeld zijn.

Het bekendst is de eerste versie van Waterhouse, uit 1888. Het schilderij bevindt zich in de collectie van Tate Britain en schijnt de bestverkopende ansichtkaart van het museum te zijn. Hier zijn we weer een stap verder in het verhaal. De Lady of Shalott zit in haar boot, nog rechtop, vlak voor haar dood. De jonkvrouw heeft haar weefwerk meegenomen, als een soort lijkwade, of als een nalatenschap aan de buitenwereld. Waterhouse geloofde blijkbaar niet dat de vloek het werk vernietigde, maar dat die het de wereld in hielp. Wat zullen mensen over haar denken als ze het doek vinden met scènes waarop ze misschien wel zelf zijn afgebeeld? Een kunstenaar, een kopiist of een voyeur?

Het voyeurisme van het kijken naar gemedieerde beelden van de wereld speelt een rol in de tapijten van hedendaagse kunstenaar Erin M. Riley. Ze weeft screenshots van Pornhub, rondslingerende smartphones en intieme zelfportretten die doen denken aan selfies. Afbeeldingen vindt ze via Google, Facebook, Instagram en Tumblr. De tapijten verwijzen naar de chatrooms waarin ze oproeide en die haar seksualiteit gevormd hebben, maar met het weven keert ze zich tegelijk ook af van de digitale wereld. ‘The images I weave are consumed and scrolled past at a speed that is maddening, but tapestry stays slow,’ zegt Riley. Het voyeurisme zit hem zowel in het gebruik van anderen die ze online observeert, als in het verbeelden van haar eigen lichaam, waarbij ze het publiek tot voyeur maakt. Als we de Lady of Shalott zien als voyeur, iemand die schaamteloos beelden van anderen gebruikt voor haar artistieke creaties, zien we aan het eind van haar verhaal een omkering: haar dode lichaam wordt een spektakel.

Tennysons twee versies van het gedicht eindigen verschillend. In het slot uit 1842 verzamelt zich een menigte rond het lichaam van de jonkvrouw. De ridders van Camelot slaan bevreesd een kruis. Eén ridder is niet bang voor het schouwspel: But Lancelot mused a little space; / He said, ‘She has a lovely face; / God in his mercy lend her grace, / The Lady of Shalott.’ Ik geef de voorkeur aan het einde uit 1832. Ook daar verzamelt de menigte zich rond het lichaam. Op de borst van de jonkvrouw vindt men een stukje beschreven perkament: ‘The web was woven curiously, / The charm is broken utterly, / Draw near and fear not,—this is I, / The Lady of Shalott.’ Ze krijgt hier tenminste zelf het laatste woord.

Wat ik nog steeds graag zou willen weten, is wat de jonkvrouw nu precies weefde, wat voor werk ze aan de wereld naliet en wat voor effect het had op mensen. Weten we eigenlijk wel zeker dat ze de beelden in de spiegel kopieert nadat ze ze gezien heeft, dat ze de buitenwereld reproduceert? Is het misschien andersom, heeft Tennyson het net verkeerd begrepen en weeft ze een wereld die vervolgens via de spiegel naar buiten wordt geprojecteerd? Dat zou haar tot Plato’s demiurg (letterlijk: ambachtsman) maken, de bouwer of schepper die het universum, inclusief goden, planeten en mensen, uit ongeordende materie vormt naar het beeld van de Ideeën.

Ik denk niet dat de vloek erop gericht is te voorkomen dat de Lady of Shalott de echte wereld zou aanschouwen, maar eerder andersom: dat men haar zou zien, levend en ongemedieerd, niet als spiegelbeeld, schaduw, verhaal of geweven voorstelling maar als schepper. Als kunstenaar is ze hoe dan ook de schepper van haar werk, en net als alle kunst is dat werk een onvolmaakte kopie van wat ze had willen uitdrukken. Zodra ze stopt met weven, heft ze ook zichzelf op, want een schepper bestaat alleen in de daad van het scheppen. Kunstenaar en kunstwerk kunnen niet in dezelfde wereld bestaan; als demiurg behoort de kunstenaar tot een andere werkelijkheid. Als ze het werk de wereld in wil sturen, moet ze zelf wijken.

De kunstenaar kan dan enkel nog gekend worden via haar beeld en gelijkenis, het kunstwerk. Zodra het de wereld in vliegt is het niet langer slechts een kopie van de wereld of van haar innerlijk, maar wordt het een onderdeel van het web van de wereld dat nieuwe schaduwen en reflecties oproept. Daar heeft de kunstenaar geen zeggenschap meer over, omdat haar rol als schepper is uitgespeeld. Misschien moest de Lady of Shalott sterven, zodat haar werk kon gaan leven.

article_text:
Holden Luntz Gallery presents Stephen Wilkes: America in Detail, Discovering Its Life and Light ; the exhibition revisits a landmark body of work made at the turn of the millennium. During a 52-day journey across the United States, Wilkes photographed the country through its people, landscapes, rituals, and unexpected moments of beauty.

Created during a period of significant change in photography, America in Detail brought together Wilkes’s instinct for narrative with a new possibility in fine art printing. Working in large-format film and later translating the images into monumental digital prints, Wilkes helped establish a new visual standard for detail, scale, and permanence. The project was among the early demonstrations of how digital printing could serve photography not merely as reproduction, but as a serious and expressive fine art medium.

Epson played a defining role in that moment. The original America in Detail project was produced during a pivotal period in the development of archival inkjet printing, when advances in pigment inks and digital imaging opened new possibilities for photographers working at ambitious scale. This exhibition, sponsored by Epson, returns to that history while underscoring the lasting importance of the print itself: its presence, materiality, tonal range, and ability to hold a viewer’s attention over time.

Rather than searching for a single definition of the country, Wilkes found its character in particulars. His photographs move between intimate human encounters and expansive landscapes, between roadside architecture and places of devotion, between private gestures and public life. Each image carries the feeling of discovery, revealing an America shaped as much by its quiet, unguarded moments as by its familiar symbols.

The series also reveals the eye that would later shape Wilkes’s celebrated Day to Night photographs, in which he builds complex, time-based compositions from thousands of exposures made from a single viewpoint. Yet America in Detail has its own immediacy. These are photographs made in motion, shaped by encounter and curiosity, attentive to the details that make a place feel inhabited and alive.

At a moment when images are more abundant than ever, Wilkes’s prints make a compelling case for sustained looking. Their scale invites viewers to move close, to notice the precision of a gesture, a horizon, a passing expression, or a seemingly incidental detail that becomes central to the picture’s emotional life. The exhibition considers photography not simply as a record of what was seen, but as an enduring way of preserving atmosphere, memory, and human connection.

Stephen Wilkes: America in Detail, Discovering Its Life and Light coincides with the twenty-fifth anniversary of the original project and arrives as the United States marks its 250th year. Together, the photographs offer both a time capsule and a reminder that the country’s most lasting portrait may be found not only in its monuments, but in the life unfolding around them.

Stephen Wilkes: America in Detail, Discovering Its Life and Light On view from October 17 through October 31, 2026 Holden Luntz Gallery 332 Worth Ave. Palm Beach, FL 33480-4617 www.holdenluntz.com

Holden Luntz Gallery invites you for coffee, sweets and an opportunity to meet the award-winning photographer STEPHEN WILKES as he shares his artistic insight with a curated collection of photographs centering on America and sponsored by Epson.

Saturday, October 24, 2026 From 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM

article_text:
写真家・佐藤信太郎の個展「都市百景」が、2026年9月1日から13日まで、東京・小伝馬町のMONO GRAPHY Camera ＆ Artで開催される。長年にわたり都市を撮影してきた佐藤の代表的な3シリーズ「夜光」「街景」「非常階段東京」を一堂に紹介する。

1969年東京生まれの佐藤は、土地が持つ性格や歴史、そこで営まれる人々の生活とともに、写真というメディアが持つ「物質性」をテーマに制作を続けてきた。本展では、平面性や解像感、圧縮感、光、色、色面といった写真固有の性質を前景化し、見慣れた都市を単なる風景ではなく、一つの「像」として捉え直す。

「夜光」が写し出すのは、東京や大阪の繁華街。無秩序に乱立しているように見える看板やネオンを切り取ることで、そこに潜む色や光、形のリズムを浮かび上がらせる。一方、「街景」では東京、千葉、大阪の街を晴天時の順光で撮影。強い光によって鮮やかさと明瞭な輪郭を獲得した都市は、奥行きを失い、芝居の書割りを思わせる平坦で非現実的な風景へと変貌する。

「非常階段東京」では、地上でも高層階でもない非常階段という「中間的な高さ」から東京を観察する。建物の裏側に面することの多い非常階段からは、普段は意識されにくい街の表情とともに、都市全体の構造と細部が同時に立ち現れる。さらに昼と夜のあわいの時間を捉えることで、その土地に固有の気配を写真のなかに定着させている。

異なる距離、光、視点によって都市へアプローチする3シリーズを横断する本展。観察と再構成を往還しながら、写真が都市の知覚そのものをいかに変化させ得るのかを探る機会となる。9月12日19:30からはギャラリートークも開催（880円）。

佐藤は2009年に日本写真協会賞新人賞、2012年に林忠彦賞を受賞。2016年には東京都写真美術館「東京・TOKYO 日本の新進作家展 vol.13」に参加し、2025年には写真集『都市の相貌』をふげん社より刊行している。
